findings.title: Concurrent reader thread is neither synchronized nor joined
findings.body: The background reader is started and group deletion proceeds immediately, with no latch confirming that a read actually started before deletion. After deletion the test only sets `deletedAll` and asserts, without joining the thread. Exceptions from reads still in flight can therefore be recorded after the assertion, so the test can pass even when the concurrent-read bug occurs. Additionally, if any `groupUuid` deletion throws, `deletedAll` is never set in a finally block and the non-daemon thread keeps issuing requests indefinitely, potentially hanging the test run. Use a startup latch, set the stop flag in a `finally`, join the thread with a timeout, and assert only after it has terminated.

findings.title: Test does not exercise the changed getSubGroupsCount path
findings.body: The reader calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, where the last argument is only `briefRepresentation`. It does not request subgroup counts. The server code only calls `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` when the `subGroupsCount` option is enabled, and `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` is the method this PR fixes. As written, the regression test can pass on the unfixed base because it never reaches the NPE path. The test should explicitly request subgroup counts or otherwise invoke `getSubGroupsCount` for groups being deleted.

findings.title: Same null-delegate NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR only adds a null guard in `getSubGroupsCount`, but the search/pagination overloads of `getSubGroupsStream` at lines 256, 262, and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. If the cached group has been deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and these methods still throw an NPE, so concurrent subgroup access remains broken. These methods should handle a missing delegate consistently, for example by returning an empty stream or delegating through the same guarded path.
